request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity and publish transition architecture, migration plan, and public usage dashboard in Q3 2026
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under public rules in Q4 2026
Serve all public API traffic from the new stack and transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domains, and associated assets to the governing entity in Q1 2027
Conduct and publish a sustainability consultation in Q2-Q3 2027
Operate the public API with at least 99% monthly uptime and publish quarterly technical and budget reports during 2027
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition administered through Intersect/CDH arrangements as described in the proposal
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed public good under an independent not-for-profit and fund 18 months of transition and operations.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets Cardano developers read from and interact with the blockchain without running their own node infrastructure.
The proposal states that Blockfrost adoption in the Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey increased from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025 and provides links for each survey year.
The proposal states that Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal says 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the commercial model difficult for financing public-good operations.

The proposal commits to transferring all Blockfrost intellectual property, including source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets, to the governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.

The proposed governance structure includes a five-seat community-approved board, with four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, stated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, allocated 79.1% to staffing, 19.3% to operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% to legal and accounting.
The proposal says unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

The proposal states that long-term sustainability after the 18-month funding period may come from not-for-profit commercial tiers or vendor-backed partner models, with future profits or fees supporting the treasury or not-for-profit operations.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to move Blockfrost from its current model into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with claimed high developer adoption, major transaction-submission dependency, IP transfer, governance formation, public reporting, and 18 months of funded operations.
